items.item_text: Degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration or related.
3+ years of direct supervisory or management experience in a healthcare setting.
5+ years of progressive healthcare operations, ambulatory clinic, or medical practice management experience.
Join one of the nation’s leading academic medical centers and play a key role in advancing world-class eye care!

The Department of Ophthalmology’s Orbital and Ophthalmic Plastic Surgery (Oculoplastics) clinic at UCLA Health is seeking a Clinic Manager to lead a skilled team of professionals in our outpatient clinic. This individual will champion operational excellence, foster team collaboration, and ensure an exceptional patient experience while supporting cutting-edge clinical care. In this role, you will:
Oversee daily clinic operations, ensuring efficiency, quality, and adherence to UCLA Health standards.
Supervise and develop administrative, clinical, and supervisory staff while promoting a collaborative, service-focused environment.
Partner with physicians and leadership to enhance workflows, patient access, and overall clinic performance.
Coordinate clinical and imaging support for faculty, fellows, optometrists, and residents.
Monitor patient satisfaction, manage escalations, oversee service recovery, and handle VIP patient coordination.
Maintain inventory and manage procurement of equipment and supplies for exam rooms, imaging labs, and visual field areas.
Review and update clinic policies and procedures to ensure compliance, consistency, and best practices.

Knowledge of ophthalmic clinic operations, patient intake, vision testing, electronic medical record documentation, and minor office procedures sufficient to provide back-up support to clinical staff as needed.
Ability to organize and manage a busy and changing clinical practice.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and follow through on assignments in a timely manner.
Ability to establish priorities, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to adapt to changing workloads, assignments, and operational needs.
Ability to supervise, motivate, and develop administrative and clinical support staff.
Ability to identify workflow issues and implement improvements to increase efficiency.
Strong interpersonal skills to maintain effective working relationships with providers, staff, patients, and leadership.
Ability to analyze problems, make sound decisions, and implement effective solutions.
Strong organizational, planning, and time management skills.
Excellent verbal, written, and telephone communication skills.
Ability to maintain effectiveness under pressure, frequent interruptions, and competing priorities.
